_readme: Settings for the in-force financial forecast (09), the actual-vs-expected variance waterfall (10) and the forecast-vintage accuracy study (11). The NPV engine does not read this file. Every value carries a status: E = estimated from experience by forecast_lib.py at run time, J = judgment awaiting Humana calibration, X = external input Humana must provide (the same letters as config/assumption_basis.json, plus X for inputs only Humana can supply). Sources of the forecast's other parameters (forecast_lib.line_params records each one's source in the output): Med Supp and D&V claim trend, rate actions, the premium age step, mortality and the payment patterns come from the approved assumption file (assumption_control.load_assumptions()). Persistency (lapse by duration and the Med Supp shock lapse) is the EXISTING book's own credibility-weighted lapse experience from this run's governance step (03b indications, status E), because the approved file holds the NEW-BUSINESS pricing basis from public sources, which describes a different population (v4.1); it falls back to the approved values only if 03b has not run. The Med Supp age slope, selection and plan relativities are the book's morbidity curves in config/claim_cost_curves.json, the same curves that normalize its experience. Medicaid churn, trend and rate update are measured from the book, because the approved file holds the NEW-STATE CONTRACT assumptions. This file and claim_cost_curves.json are covered by the approval hash (assumption_control.GOVERNED_CONFIGS).

eligibility_lag_months._note: Months between the last eligibility month in the extract and the claims paid-through month (synthetic: eligibility 2025-12, paid through 2026-02). The forecast starts the month after the last eligibility month. Vintages reconstructed in synthetic mode keep the same gap.

completion._note: Bornhuetter-Ferguson for incurred months with 0..bf_max_lag months of run-out, chain ladder (the SQL kit's method: volume-weighted age-to-age factors over the latest 18 incurred months, lags 8+ grouped, tail 1.00) for older months. The BF a-priori PMPM is a log-linear trend fitted to the line's completed PMPM over incurred months with at least apriori_min_observable_lag months of run-out within the latest apriori_window_months, projected forward. Production: the a-priori is normally the approved forecast PMPM for the month.

base_period_months._note: Latest completed incurred months used as the claims base.

credibility._note: Full credibility n = 1082 x (1 + CV^2) claims (90% probability of being within 5%, ASOP 25), CV = severity coefficient of variation measured from the segment's line. Segment = state x plan (Med Supp, D&V) or state x rate cell (Medicaid). The complement is the manual relativity: Med Supp plan, age and duration factors from config/claim_cost_curves.json; D&V plan and Medicaid rate cell at their premium (capitation) relativity, i.e. a loss-ratio-neutral complement, which is how a rating manual or state rate cell would price them.

pooling_charge._note: Charge for claims above the pooling point (Med Supp $50K, D&V $10K, Medicaid $250K) added to pooled incurred. Credibility-weighted by limited fluctuation (ASOP 25): Z = min(1, sqrt(n_large / n_full)), n_large = claims above the pooling point, n_full = 1082 x (1 + CV^2) with CV the coefficient of variation of the excess severity (the charge is an aggregate, as for the segment claims base; CV = default_excess_cv when fewer than 2 large claims); complement = judgment charge (no public figure for these pooling points). Sensitivity: Medicaid 0.5%-2.0%. Production: Humana's large-claim study.

new_sales._note: Synthetic default (v4.1): the trailing-12-month new issues per month (Medicaid: new enrollees) with that period's mix of state, plan / rate cell, issue age and first-month premium, grown at the observed year-over-year growth of new issues (last 12 vs prior 12 months, capped at +/-30%) from the trailing window's midpoint. The v4 flat average lagged a growing book (Med Supp member months biased -0.9% across vintages). Production: the Finance sales plan by line and month (plan_by_line_per_month), used as given.

MEDSUPP._note: Approved annual_rate_increase applied each January (the experience shows premium stepping in January). Production: the rate-filing plan by state.

MEDICAID._note: The latest January step in book capitation for continuing members (the state rate year). The approved 4.5% is the new-state contract, not this book. Production: the state rate certification.

medsupp_premium_age_step._note: premium_age_step from the approved file, applied continuously by month of attained age (the experience premium moves with attained age every month).

redetermination_wave._note: Calendar window of the post-PHE eligibility unwinding (production: the state's redetermination calendar). Base churn is measured on months outside the window. When the window overlaps the forecast, churn inside it = base x multiplier, estimated from at least 3 observed window months to the as-of date, otherwise the default (judgment, deliberately not the synthetic generator's value).

seasonality._note: Month-of-year factors from a log-linear fit of completed PMPM with month dummies on mature months, used only if the dummies are jointly significant (F-test). The synthetic book has no seasonality, so the test is expected to reject it.

ae._note: Variance waterfall: the forecast made at the vintage (data cut at that eligibility month and its paid-through month) against actual experience of the comparison year on current data. Production: the prior cycle's vintage from the registry.

vintages._note: A forecast month is scored only once it has at least 3 months of claim run-out at the current paid-through date (completion at or above about 92%), so scoring is not dominated by IBNR estimates. Production registry: NPV_VINTAGE_DIR or <output>/vintage_registry, never cleared by the clean start.
